newsitem.title: USA: US agency seeks more older women for health study.
newsitem.headline: US agency seeks more older women for health study.

text.p: The National Institutes of Health said Wednesday it is looking for nearly 100,000 more women, primarily those over age 60, to participate in a 10-year study of women's health.
Researchers expect to reach the goal of 164,000 women participants by spring 1998 but have had more success recruiting women age 50-59 than their older counterparts.

The study aims to find out whether post-menopausal women age 50-79 need to take oestrogen and vitamins to protect against bone loss and whether low-fat diets help prevent heart attacks and breast and colon cancer.

The Women's Health Initiative study got underway in 1993, partially in response to the exclusion of women in earlier health studies on medications for heart disease and cancer. Final results will not be available until 2007.

About 64,000 of the participants will be in three active tests for effectiveness of low-fat diets, vitamin D and calcium and oestrogen hormone replacements. The rest will be followed for their medical histories and health habits.
